Section 1 Introduction and Safety Introduction and Safety Introduction Read this manual thoroughly and understand all of the instructions, cautions, and warnings before using this equipment. If any section of the manual is not understood, contact your nearest Independent Authorized Service Dealer, or contact Generac Customer Service at 1-888-GENERAC (1-888-436-3722), or www.generac.com with any questions or concerns. The owner is responsible for proper maintenance and safe use of the equipment. Before operating on or servicing this engine: • Study all warnings in this manual and on the prod- uct carefully. • Become familiar with this manual and the unit before use. • Refer to the Assembly section of the manual for instructions on final assembly procedures. Follow the instructions completely. Save these instructions for future reference. ALWAYS supply this manual to any individual that will use this machine. THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN WAS BASED ON MACHINES IN PRODUCTION AT THE TIME OF PUBLICATION. GENERAC RESERVES THE RIGHT TO MODIFY THIS MANUAL AT ANY TIME. Safety Rules The manufacturer cannot anticipate every possible circumstance that might involve a hazard. The warnings in this manual, and on tags and decals affixed to the unit are, therefore, not all inclusive. If using a procedure, work method or operating technique that the manufacturer does not specifically recommend, verify that it is safe for others. Also make sure the procedure, work method or operating technique utilized does not render the equipment unsafe. Throughout this publication, and on tags and decals affixed to the engine, DANGER, WARNING, CAUTION and NOTE blocks are used to alert personnel to special instructions about a particular operation that may be hazardous if performed incorrectly or carelessly. Section 3 Assembly and Installation Assembly and Installation Assemble Cylinder Block Grouping and Mark Positions of Cylinder Bores Under regular production conditions, the diameter tolerance of cylinder block is 0.002 in (0.04 mm) and the cylinder bores fall into four groups. In special cases, increasing cylinder bore diameter is permissible. The cylinder bore diameter tolerance for production and repair is 0.001 in (0.03 mm) and the cylinder bores fall into three groups. When a cylinder bore has been reworked to repair dimension, the other three cylinder bores should be machined to the dimensions for production and repair. Grouping Marks on Cylinder Block Install Main Bearing Cap The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 and an arrow are cast on each main bearing cap. Install starting from front sequentially. The arrow points to front end face of cylinder block. Width of 1, 2, 4 and 5 main bearing caps are same but No. 3 main bearing cap is wider than the others. Right lower edge of No. 3 main bearing cap requires chamfer. Main bearing caps are positioned by rabbets. Dimensions of a rabbet are not centered so as to prevent installation in opposite direction. Main Bearing Cap Dimensions Long Side 2.27 in (57.7 mm) Short Side 2.18 in (55.3 mm) Main bearing cap rabbet and cylinder block main bearing cap rabbet are in interference fit with a magnitude of interference of 0.001–0.006 in (0.025–0.145 mm). 1. Wipe up the mating faces on main bearing caps and cylinder block with clean no-woven fabric or silk cloth before installation. 2. After assembly, side planes of No.1 and No.5 main bearing caps should be flush with front and rear end faces of cylinder block or below them. Install Main Bearing Cap Bolts There are nine main bearing cap bolts and one main bearing cap stud. For a transverse engine, the stud is installed in LH side threaded hole (when viewed from front) on No. 2 main bearing cap for mounting oil strainer bracket. For a longitudinal engine, it is installed in LH side threaded hole (when viewed from front) on No. 4 main bearing cap. 1. Apply engine oil to mating faces at heads of main bearing cap bolts. 2. Hand-tighten main bearing cap bolts and main bearing cap stud first, and then tighten them to 797–885 in-lbs (90–100 Nm). NOTE: If any bolt cannot be screwed in by hand, back it out to locate the cause, replace with a new bolt, or check the bolt hole. 3. After machining of main bearing holes, clean and blow-dry cylinder block thoroughly. Under regular production conditions, a main bearing hole has only one dimension and will not be grouped. The dimension can be increased by 0.02 in (0.40 mm) for production and repair purposes. The five main bearing holes should be increased at the same time. Stamp size marking of main bearing hole at C in Figure 3-1 to show distinction (increase by 0.02 in (0.40 mm) after dimensioning). Press-Fit of Bowl Plug 1. Apply Loctite™ 648 sealant around circumference of bowl plug. 2. Drive bowl plug into corresponding hole on cylinder block with a special tool until bowl plug is 0.00– 0.02 in (0–0.50 mm) below cylinder block. 1.5L Gaseous Engine Service Manual 5

2. After dowel pin is fitted properly, spray engine oil on the connecting rod body, cap and threaded mating faces. 3. Screw on a connecting rod nut by hand and tighten in two steps with a torque wrench: • 150–204 in-lbs (20±3 Nm) • 266–318 in-lbs (33±3 Nm) Install Piston Ring The top piston ring is rectangular, the second gas ring is tapered, and the oil ring is a compound steel band ring. 1. Spray engine oil on piston ring grooves and pistons. NOTE: Leave the face having words on the top ring upwards and the outer notch on the second ring downwards. 2. When installing oil ring, fit expanders into corresponding oil grooves first. 3. Install the two scrapers. Stagger gaps of the two oil ring scrapers and laps of expanders for 90°, and let the upper and lower scrapers form a 180° angle. 4. Install second gas ring. 5. Install top ring. Stagger the two gas rings and the upper scraper gap for 120°. When installing a ring, use a special tapered sleeve with a maximum diameter 0.04 in (1 mm) larger than diameter of corresponding piston head, so that the piston ring can rotate freely without seizure. The clearances are as follows: Side Clearance of Piston Ring 1st Ring Groove 0.00 in (0.04–0.08 mm) 2nd Ring Groove 0.00 in (0.03–0.07 mm) Oil Ring Groove 0.00–0.01 in (0.03–0.16 mm) Gap Clearance of Piston Ring 1st Ring Groove 0.01 in (0.20–0.35 mm) 2nd Ring Groove 0.02 in (0.40–0.55 mm) Oil Ring Groove 0.01–0.02 in (0.20–0.60 mm) Assemble Oil Baffle Install an oil baffle assembly to the right side of tail of cylinder block (when viewed from front). The tension spring of the oil baffle assembly should be below the oil pan flange on cylinder block. Install Main Bearing Shell As required by after service, three types of main bearing shells for repair purpose are available: 1. One is for the main bearing hole oversized by 0.02 in (0.4 mm) and has a black mark in addition to “0.4” stamped on the steel back. 1.5L Gaseous Engine Service Manual Assembly and Installation 2. One is for the crankshaft journal undersized by 0.01 in (0.25 mm) and has a green mark in addition to the mark stamped on the steel back. 3. One is used to correct bearing clearance when former bearing shell generates too much noise, and has a yellow mark in addition to “0.02” stamped on the steel back. Install Connecting Rod Bearing Shell Two types of connecting rod bearing shells for repair purpose are available: 1. One is for the crankshaft journal undersized by 0.01 in (0.25 mm) and has a green mark in addition to “0.25” stamped on the steel back. 2. One is used to correct bearing clearance when former bearing shell generates too loud noise and has a yellow mark in addition to “0.025” stamped on the steel back. When assembling, align oil grooves and oil holes on upper main bearing shell with the oil holes on cylinder block, and verify the following: • There are no oil holes on lower main bearing shell. • Upper and lower connecting rod bearing shells can be interchanged. • Upper and lower connecting rod bearing shells have no oil grooves but each has an oil hole. • Use a set of connecting rod bearing shells and main bearing shells from the same supplier. • Before installation, apply engine oil on connecting rod bearing shells and inner surfaces of main bearing shells. • Keep back surfaces of bearing shells clean. Install Crankshaft, Crankshaft Woodruff Key and Crankshaft Thrust Plate Crankshaft key groove and crankshaft woodruff key are in transition fit in width with a magnitude of interference of 0–0.002 in (0–0.051 mm). After a woodruff key is fitted in, protrusion height should be 0.055–0.0685 in (1.392– 1.739 mm). Install two crankshaft thrust plates on front and rear thrust surfaces of the cylinder block. 1. Apply engine oil to each thrust plate. The side without oil groove should face cylinder block and the side with oil groove should face crankshaft. 2. Apply engine oil on main journal, connecting rod journals and thrust surfaces. Fit clearance of connecting rod bearing Fit clearance of main bearing 0.000–0.002 in (0.006–0.06 mm) 0.000–0.002 in (0.011–0.058 mm) 3. Measure axial clearance of crankshaft. Clearance should be within 0.004–0.012 in (0.093–0.303 mm). Measure rotating torque of crankshaft. Rotating 7

After installing cylinder head without spark plugs, rotating torque of crankshaft should be less than 274 in-lbs (31 Nm) after crankshaft rotates a maximum of six turns. Install Oil Pump, Crankshaft Front Oil Seal and Oil Strainer Assemble Front Oil Seal 1. Install oil pump onto press-fit fixture. The face with the part number should be outside. 2. Press crankshaft front oil seal in place. Check oil seal edge for damage and defects. Magnitude of interference between front oil seal and oil pump housing: 0.01–0.02 in (0.26–0.50 mm). Install Oil Pump with Front Oil Seal Assembly 1. Install oil pump onto cylinder block. 2. Hand-tighten the two bolts. 3. Hand-tighten the other four bolts after the process guide pin is removed. 4. Tighten oil pump bolts to 71–97 in-lbs (8–11 Nm). 5. Measure flatness between oil pump bottom plane and oil pan flange on cylinder block, which should be ±0.01 in (±0.26 mm). Install Oil Strainer Assembly 1. Install oil strainer gasket onto oil pump inlet flange. 2. Install oil strainer assembly. 3. Hand-tighten the two oil strainer flange washer bolts. 4. Tighten an oil strainer bracket onto cylinder block using a bolt. Put bracket over the stud on the left side of No. 2 main bearing cap. 5. Hand-tighten nut after installing a plain washer. 6. Tighten oil strainer flange bolts to 71–106 in-lbs (8–12 Nm). 7. Tighten bracket bolt to 150–204 in-lbs (17–23 Nm). 8. Oil strainer assembly should be installed onto cylinder block and oil pump freely. If any stress is found during assembly, replace it. Assemble Water Pump 1. Install two process guide pins on front face of cylinder block. 2. Fit a water pump gasket through the process guide pins and install water pump assembly onto cylinder block. 3. Remove process guide pins. 4. Hand-tighten the four water pump bolts and tighten to 71–97 in-lbs (8–11 Nm). NOTE: Water pump gear and pump impeller should rotate freely. Install Rear Oil Seal Retainer and Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal 1. Before assembling rear oil seal retainer with rear oil seal assembly, apply engine oil on rear oil seal edge or crankshaft rear oil seal journal. 2. Stretch edge with a special tool, keeping the oil seal edge clear of the tool to avoid damage. 3. Install two process guide pins on rear end face of cylinder block. 4. Fit a rear oil seal retainer onto cylinder block through the process guide pins. 5. Install rear oil seal retainer with rear oil seal assembly onto cylinder block using positioner. 6. Hand-tighten two bolts. 7. Remove the process guide pins and tighten the other two bolts. 8. Tighten the four bolts to 71–97 in-lbs (8–11 Nm). 9. Measure flatness between rear oil seal retainer bottom plane and oil pan flange on cylinder block, which should be within ±0.01 in (±0.26 mm). Assemble Cylinder Head Install Valve Seat Ring Intake and exhaust valve seat rings and corresponding cylinder head holes are in interference fit with a magnitude of interference of 0.003–0.004 in (0.078–0.11 mm). 1. Before pressing valve seat rings, wash cylinder head and blow-clean valve seat ring holes with high pressure air. 2. Soak valve seat rings in a liquid nitrogen tank for at least ten minutes. 3. Remove valve seat rings from liquid nitrogen tank and press them in cylinder head using a special tool. NOTE: The valve seat rings must be pressed into place without clearance between bottom of each seat ring hole and corresponding valve seat ring. 4. Check seating condition of each valve seat ring. 001089 Figure 3-6. Press-Fitting Bowl Plugs in Cylinder Head A Water jacket cleaning holes 4. After machining and washing cylinder head, press bowl plugs in to seal them. 5. Apply Loctite™ 648 sealant around circumferences of bowl plugs and press them into the mounting holes on cylinder head using a special tool. NOTE: After being pressed in, bowl plugs should be 0.00–0.02 in (0–0.5 mm) below chamfer surfaces of corresponding holes on cylinder head. Install Intake and Exhaust Valve There are two intake valves and two exhaust valves on each cylinder. Among these valves, area of intake valve head is larger than that of exhaust valve head. 1. Remove No. 1 bearing cap and No. 2–No. 5 bearing caps and put them in order. 2. Verify that burrs produced during machining have been removed completely. Check cylinder head and camshaft cover for damage. 3. Clean all oil passages and inner chambers on cylinder head. Verify all oil passages are unobstructed and there are no burrs at joints of oil passages. 1.5L Gaseous Engine Service Manual 9

Assembly and Installation Install Valve Spring Lower Seat 4. Slide valve spring lower seat (bottom plane faces cylinder head) into valve guide. Valve spring lower seat bottom plane should stick to the machined surface on valve spring lower seat on cylinder head. Install Valve Oil Seal 5. Apply lubricating oil on lip of each valve oil seal and install valve oil seal assemblies onto corresponding valve guides. 6. Tap valve guides using pressing sleeve and hammer to fit oil seals in place. Verify oil seals and valve guides fit in position. 7. Tilt cylinder head to wipe up intake and exhaust valves and valve seat rings using fabric or silk cloth. 8. Apply engine oil to valve stems. 9. Fit intake and exhaust valves into cylinder head.
